title: Longest Even Odd Subarray With Threshold

constraints.impact: Even O(n²) or O(n³) is fast enough here, so brute force passes. The sliding window is still the clean O(n) answer, and it is what an interviewer wants to see. The answer can be 0: n ≥ 1 does not mean a valid subarray exists.

constraints.meaning: Every value is a small positive number.
constraints.impact: No overflow and no negative numbers, so nums[i] % 2 is always 0 (even) or 1 (odd) in every language.

constraints.meaning: threshold is in the same range as the values.
constraints.impact: A value can be bigger than threshold. Such a value can never be inside a valid subarray, so it cuts the array into separate parts.

constraints.text: nums[l] is even, parity alternates, every value ≤ threshold (statement)
constraints.meaning: The subarray starts with an even value, then odd, even, odd, … and no value is above threshold.
constraints.impact: Each rule only looks at one element or two neighbours. When a rule breaks at index right, no valid window can cross it, so the window restarts there instead of shrinking one step at a time.

bruteForce.summary: try every start l with an even value ≤ threshold, extend r to the right while the next value is ≤ threshold and has the other parity, and keep the longest length. O(n²) time. It passes for n ≤ 100, but it checks the same elements again for every start.
